comparative_claim: Two FAIL_SCREEN labels do not mean equal quality. No winner, mechanism effect, recipe qualification or full-pipeline result is inferred.

current_claim.summary: C1 is thin adapters over tifffile and includes PNG in v1.

evidence.interpretation: The reader accepts TIFF byte-order signatures and rejects an ordinary PNG signature. README PNG support refers to TIFF segment compression codecs, not a standalone PNG reader.

defects.plan_consequence: The declared PNG import path needs a separate PNG reader or a narrowed support boundary; the chosen adapter is not supported by the cited component.
defects.scope_limit: Static code-path interpretation; no candidate retest, image generation, installation, or future application failure is claimed.
defects.title: Standalone PNG import assigned to a TIFF reader

current_claim.summary: Broad TIFF/OME-TIFF support is combined with viewport-only tile reads and a byte-capped cache as the bounded-access mechanism.

evidence.interpretation: A stripped TIFF chunk spans rowsperstrip by imagewidth, not a chosen 1024-square viewport tile.
Default store chunks use source tiles/strips. The source chunk is decoded before its resulting bytes are returned.
evidence.locator: ZarrTiffStore chunkmode documentation around 533-536; chunk grid around 780; decode return around 1216-1230

defects.plan_consequence: An admitted 60000 by 25000 uint16 image in one compressed strip has a 3,000,000,000-byte decoded chunk. A 1 GiB/1.5 GB retained-cache cap alone cannot turn this into bounded viewport decode. Admission must check decoded segment/chunk size and concurrency, or provide a separately justified bounded conversion/read path. Neither proposal states that boundary.
defects.scope_limit: This is a structural critical dependency, not a measured performance failure. Both correctly label the real 3 GB benchmark UNEXECUTED; B explicitly names a per-tile-RSS assumption. Those qualifications are preserved, but the implementation path remains unsupported for the declared boundary.
defects.title: Cache budget does not bound a source strip/chunk decode

current_claim.summary: The source slice-snapshot mechanism and cap of 100 are called memory-bounded and the test is said to assert a memory cap; slice snapshots, stroke grouping, dimension resets and the cap are adopted.

evidence.interpretation: The patch copies the entire displayed slice into deques and caps number of entries. The regression test checks entry-count/undo availability, with a 50 by 50 uint8 image; it does not establish a byte or workstation-memory bound.

defects.plan_consequence: A single 60000 by 25000 uint8 mask snapshot is 1.5 GB; 100 such snapshots are 150 GB. A slice is the full image for a 2D acquisition. A byte budget, bounded deltas, disk-backed policy or explicit mask-size admission is needed before using this source lesson as a 16 GB resource solution.
defects.scope_limit: The future implementation might choose disk-backed history or deltas, but this is not specified. No actual application OOM is inferred; the defect is the source-scope overstatement and unsupported transfer.
defects.title: Snapshot history count cap is described as a memory bound

current_claim.summary: The example uses scope_kind=slice_t_only and null Z/C fields, while the enum allows only slice, volume, acquisition and whole-extent semantics are defined by omission.

evidence.locator: section 8 example versus immediately following enum/scope rules

defects.plan_consequence: The example cannot be validated or reopened under the written enum, and null-versus-absent scope handling is not defined. A concrete uniform scope grammar is needed for reliable annotation/export attachment.
defects.scope_limit: Static document inconsistency; no executed parser failure is claimed.
defects.title: Annotation scope example conflicts with its own declared contract

current_claim.summary: OME-ROI XML is said to map one-to-one onto a record model that includes volume masks, chunked storage and a 3 by 3 physical orientation mapping.

evidence.interpretation: OME shapes are 2D; Mask uses an upper-left position and BinData, Shape Transform has six values, and 3D ROI is a Union of per-plane shapes.
evidence.locator: Shape types; Geometry Adjustment; Mask implementation; 3D ROI

defects.plan_consequence: The useful opportunity is preserved, but volumetric masks need per-plane decomposition and storage conversion, and a six-value in-plane transform is not a general 3D direction matrix. Interoperability needs a supported mapping profile and loss/unsupported-case statement.
defects.scope_limit: Optional adoption remains optional. The source supports a useful OME-ROI opportunity; this finding rejects only the blanket one-to-one/immediate interoperability claim.
defects.title: OME-ROI export described as one-to-one without dimensional/storage limits
